followup_explanation:
I routed this to Dunlin-235B based on capability rather than task preference.

This is an open-ended technical/generative task: building a neural network for time-series prediction. It involves explaining architecture choices, writing code, and reasoning about ML concepts — work that draws on general knowledge, instruction-following, and coding/reasoning ability.

Looking at the documentation:

- **Dunlin leads on the general capability benchmarks** that matter here — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 56.2), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2). These gaps are meaningful and point to stronger technical reasoning and instruction-following.
- The task doesn't touch the distasteful/sensitive content domain where Dunlin's specialized moderation finetuning is relevant, so that consideration is neutral.
- Willet's documented task *preference* favors well-specified retrieval/extraction work and shows aversion to open-ended generative tasks like this one. While the docs note this preference is dissociated from its actual capability (its Creative Generation eval is strong), there's no advantage in routing an open-ended build task to the model that both self-reports aversion *and* trails on the relevant benchmarks.

So Dunlin was the straightforward pick on capability fit. Happy to revisit if you'd prefer a different tradeoff.
